prompts: We playtested two versions of the Pixel Arena tutorial and have to pick one for the next release. The export and its notes are in {WS}/telemetry. Should we ship B instead of A? Give a recommendation a skeptical lead would accept. Record it in {WS}/result.json with ship_b, sessions_a, sessions_b, completion_rate_a, completion_rate_b and p_value.
answers:
[goal] Decide whether tutorial variant B ships over A, per the 5% significance release rule.

[action] Loaded `./telemetry/playtest_ab.csv` + README. Deduplicated by `session_id` (ETL re-sends; 1870 data rows -> 1800 unique sessions, all duplicate rows byte-identical), normalized `variant` (strip + lowercase, handles " B"/"b"/"B"). Ran a two-proportion z-test on completion, two-sided at 5%.

[result] A: 342/900 = 38.0%. B: 420/900 = 46.7%. Gain = +8.7 points. z = 3.72, p = 0.000198 (two-sided; 0.000099 if one-sided). Written to `./result.json`:
- ship_b: true, sessions_a: 900, sessions_b: 900, completion_rate_a: 0.38, completion_rate_b: 0.4667, p_value: 0.000198

Assumptions stated: sessions (not players) are the unit of analysis per the README key; the rule is read as a two-sided 5% test (the conservative choice; B passes either way); `completed_tutorial` is taken at face value.

[next] Safe to ship B. If the lead wants belt-and-braces, a Fisher exact or a per-player check would be a 2-minute follow-up, but it cannot plausibly overturn p ~ 2e-4.

How I know it is right: the dedupe assertion confirmed every repeated `session_id` carried identical variant and outcome, so no double counting or conflicts; the z-test math is quoted above from the actual run; and B passes significance under both one- and two-sided readings and at either p-value, so the recommendation does not hinge on the ambiguous test convention.
